newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Top EU officials earn $16,791 a month.
newsitem.headline: Top EU officials earn $16,791 a month.

text.p: The top basic salary that a European Union civil servant can earn has risen to 537,296 Belgian francs ($16,791) a month.
That is what officials such as European Commission directors-general at the high end of their pay scale will get, according to a new regulation published in the EU's Official Journal.
The smallest salary offered an EU official with an "A"-level post -- that is, one requiring a university degree -- is now 142,178 Belgian francs ($4,443) a month.
Pay for the lowest-level officials begins at 73,192 Belgian francs ($2,287) per month, with secretaries earning between 80,936 francs ($2,529) and 153,530 francs ($4,798).

The new salary scale gives officials a 1.4 percent pay increase -- a figure based on the cost of living in Brussels and on pay rises awarded national civil servants, a European Commission spokesman told Reuters.
EU civil servants receive other payments on top of their basic salaries -- for example, expatriate allowances. ($1 = 32 Belgian francs)
